svg.data-vd-steps: [[0, "Metallic bonding: a lattice of positive metal ions in a sea of delocalised electrons that move freely and randomly."], [4, "Apply a potential difference: the delocalised electrons drift towards the positive terminal, carrying a current. Metals are good conductors."], [9, "Apply a force: whole layers of ions slide over each other. The sea of electrons keeps them bonded, so metals are malleable and ductile."]]
svg.title: Metallic bonding
svg.desc: Positive metal ions in a regular lattice surrounded by delocalised electrons. Play: electrons move randomly, drift when a voltage is applied, and the layers slide when a force is applied.
svg.text: A 2D slice of a metal lattice. Ions and electrons not to scale.

g.data-info: Outer electrons are free to move through the whole lattice. Metallic bonding = attraction between the cations and the delocalised electrons.
Arranged in a regular lattice of layers. Each atom has given its outer electrons to the shared sea.
With a p.d. across the metal, the delocalised electrons drift towards the positive end: metals conduct electricity (and heat).

g.text: electrons drift → towards +: an electric current

g.data-info: Layers of ions can slide over each other; the electrons still hold them together, so the metal bends or stretches instead of breaking: malleable and ductile.

g.text: layers slide; bonding remains: malleable and ductile
